chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakūnī:
That ʿAlī عليه السلام passed by a female animal and a male mounting her in the middle of the road, so he turned his face away from it.
So it was said to him: Why did you do that, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn?
He said: “It is not appropriate that you do what they do, and it is among the objectionable matters, unless you conceal it where no man or woman sees it.”

key_terms.السَّكُونِيِّ: al-Sakūnī, the narrator to whom this report is attributed
key_terms.الْمُنْكَرِ: that which is objectionable or improper
key_terms.تُوَارُوهُ: you conceal it or hide it
key_terms.ظَهْرِ الطَّرِيقِ: the open middle or surface of the road

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام teach about openly exposing animal mating in public?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام turned his face away when passing an animal mating openly on the road. He then taught that exposing such acts publicly is objectionable and that they should be concealed from the sight of men and women, indicating an ethic of public modesty and decorum.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4655 - In the narration of Al-Sakooni,
it is reported that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) passed by an animal and a stud mating in the middle of the road, and Imam (as) turned his face away.
It was said to him: "Why did you do that, O Commander of the Faithful (as)?"
Imam (as) replied: "It is not appropriate for you to do what they do (i.e., allow such things publicly). It is among the unacceptable acts unless you conceal it where no man or woman can see it."
